D005-D018_h001.question: It's been about two months now, and things just keep getting stranger. I feel like I'm constantly on edge, and my restaurant, which I've poured my life into, feels more like a cage. Lately, I’ve started feeling crawling sensations on my skin, like bugs, but there’s never anything there. It's unsettling. And the thoughts... I know it sounds crazy, but I truly believe I’m destined for something much bigger than this, that I have a special purpose, almost like I'm being guided to protect people. It's a strong feeling, like I have some hidden power. It all seems to stem from that night, when the fire alarm went off and I was trapped in the freezer for hours. Now, sometimes, I'm right back there, feeling the cold, smelling the smoke, hearing the sirens, and it's so real, like I'm reliving it – I can even feel the icy walls on my skin. I know it’s just in my head, a flashback, but it’s so vivid. I just can't shake it.
D005-D018_h001.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D005-D018_h002.question:
It's been about two months now, and things just feel… off. Like, I’ll be on a job site, wiring up a panel, and I’ll catch a flicker, a movement out of the corner of my eye. It's usually him, the guy from the accident. Not fully there, more like a hazy outline, but it’s real enough to make me jump. Then, everything just clicks together in a terrifying way. I’ll hear a foreman shouting, or a drill start up, and in my head, it’s not just noise anymore. It’s like they're talking to me, about me, about what happened. It’s almost like they know, and they’re setting me up or something.

I keep reliving the whole thing, the smell of burnt rubber, the twisted metal, the screaming. It blasts into my mind and it's like I’m right back there, seeing it all unfold again, even though I'm standing in a perfectly safe kitchen. The doctors said it was a bad accident, a traumatic brain injury, but it feels like more than that. I know those visual flickers and the feeling that everyone's somehow connected to it stems from that day, it's just been a constant playback since. I can't shake the feeling that every little random thing is a sign, pointing back to that moment, confirming that it wasn't just a random event. Sometimes, it’s like the accident never really ended.
D005-D018_h002.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D005-D018_h003.question:
It's been... I don't even know anymore, maybe two months? Everything just feels so messed up. I manage a cosmetics store, and you'd think it's all glitz and glam, but my boyfriend, Mark, I just know he's cheating. I see it in how he glances at his phone, how he’s a few minutes late from work – little things that just scream he’s with someone else. And the voices... I hear them, especially when I’m alone at home. They’re usually whispering, gossiping about me and Mark, making nasty suggestions. They tell me he's with someone prettier, someone better.

It all started after that awful night, you know, when I was robbed at the store. I still see it happen again, sometimes so vividly it's like it's real, like the robber's right in front of me again, yelling, and that's when the voices really get loud, echoing what he said, twisting it. It’s like a replay, but worse, with these awful whispers layered over it. I just can't shake the feeling that everyone's judging me, especially after what happened. I’m exhausted all the time and jumpy, like the next bad thing is always about to happen.
D005-D018_h003.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D005-D018_h004.question: It’s been pretty rough these past two months, ever since… the incident at work. I try to put it behind me, but I keep reliving the mid-air collision. Sometimes I'll catch a whiff of burning jet fuel, even when I'm just sitting at home, nowhere near an airport. And then, there’s this unnerving feeling that the news reports, the way people are looking at me, even the headlines on the TV – they all seem to be talking about me, pointing fingers. I know it sounds strange, connecting it all back to what happened, but it's like the world is suddenly focused on my mistakes. I just can't shake the images of the crash, the sounds, even the smell. It feels so real, like it’s happening all over again.
D005-D018_h004.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D005-D018_h005.question: "Lately, it's been a real struggle just to get through the day, Doc. For the past two months, I've had these flashes, you know? Like I'm right back there, in that collapsing stairwell a year and a half ago, scrambling to make sure everyone got out. It’s so vivid, I can feel the dust and debris hitting me, almost like something’s crawling on my skin. And then there's this… well, it’s embarrassing to say, but I get these strong feelings that my old high school sweetheart, who I haven't seen in decades, is totally in love with me. Like she's trying to send me messages through the TV. I know it sounds crazy, but it’s so real. It’s all tied to the accident, I swear, everything started after that building collapse. I keep thinking about it, keep dreaming about it. I just can’t shake it.”
D005-D018_h005.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D005-D018_h006.question: It's been about seven months now that things have felt… off. Ever since my husband passed, I see him sometimes, just for a flash, but it’s so realistic, like he’s right there, reaching for me. These aren’t just memories; it feels like it's happening right now. I don't feel joy in anything anymore. The things I used to love, like gardening or even just watching my favorite shows, it all just feels… empty. I go through the motions at work, cleaning houses, but it’s hard to focus. I catch myself doing strange things, like pausing in the middle of dusting to just stare at a spot on the wall for a long time, or moving my hands in an odd, repetitive way. I also feel like Mrs. Henderson, one of my clients, is talking about me behind my back, or leaving notes that are actually coded messages for me. It’s silly, I know, but I can’t shake the feeling that people are out to get me, or at least observing me too closely.
D005-D018_h006.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Delusional Disorder

D005-D018_h007.question:
"It’s been almost seven months now, since... the incident. I was mugged on my way home from school, and honestly, things just haven't been right since. It’s hard to talk about. Sometimes, I hear things, see things, almost like I'm reliving it. It's like a movie playing right before my eyes, and I can smell the fear, feel the cold of the weapon, even though I know it's not real anymore. I know it sounds crazy, but it’s like my mind can’t let go of that moment.

Other times, I get these strange urges, little movements, like I'm constantly adjusting my shirt or tapping my foot, almost like I'm trying to distract myself. It's embarrassing, especially around the kids. I feel like I have these special abilities now, like I can sense danger before it happens, or I’m super attuned to people’s intentions. It’s a strange feeling, like I’m meant for something bigger, something important. And talking… it's just so difficult. I find myself just nodding along, having less and less to say. It's not like me. I used to be so chatty with my students and their parents, but now, the words just don't come out easily."
D005-D018_h007.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Delusional Disorder

D005-D018_h008.question: "Well, doctor, it's been about seven months now that I just don't feel like myself. After my husband passed, I started volunteering more at the community center, trying to keep busy, but it’s like a chore. Nothing brings me joy anymore, not even my grandchildren's visits. Sometimes, I find myself just rocking back and forth for no reason, almost involuntarily, for long stretches. The really disturbing part, though, is how things started to change after that car accident I witnessed, the one where the young boy was hit. I keep seeing it, feeling like I'm right back there, smelling the smoke, hearing the screams, even when I know I'm sitting in my living room. It’s so vivid, like I’m reliving it. And then, at other times, a strange feeling comes over me, like I’m the only one who can truly understand the secrets of the universe, like I have some hidden knowledge. I know it sounds silly, but it feels so real, like I’m special in a significant way. Those visions and feelings, they definitely started after the accident, that’s when everything really shifted."
D005-D018_h008.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Delusional Disorder

D005-D018_h009.question:
It’s been rough, honestly. My mind just isn’t working right. Over the past seven months, I’ve felt like I’m losing my grip. I keep seeing things, usually flashes of that car crash, almost like it’s happening again right in front of me. Sometimes when those episodes hit, everything just stops. I’ll just stand there, can't move, can't even tell you what's going on around me. And talking? I barely do anymore. What’s the point?

I know it sounds strange, but I also started to think I have some kind of special power from surviving the accident, like I’m invincible or chosen for something big. Like nothing can hurt me now. It's a weird mix, all this stuff happening since the crash. It really feels like it all started after that, like my brain just broke.
D005-D018_h009.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Delusional Disorder

D005-D018_h010.question:
"Well, doctor, it's been about seven months now that things have felt… off. I've always had a pretty dark job, cleaning up after the worst, but after that last call – the one with the whole family, you know – it's like something in my head just broke. I keep seeing it all again, those images just flash right in front of me, like I’m right back there, smelling it, hearing things. It’s like a movie playing, but I’m actually in it, even though I know I’m safe.

Sometimes, it feels like the whole world is just falling apart around me, like everything is pointless because it's all going to be destroyed anyway. And I know it sounds silly, but sometimes I just find myself giggling, or acting all childish, especially when I'm under stress. It’s like I can’t control it, even though I know it’s totally inappropriate for a man my age. I've also been finding it harder to talk, you know? Like, I just don't have much to say, and when people ask me things, I just give them short answers because I can't think of anything else. It's like my words have just… dried up. It’s definitely since that incident, though. All of this, it really ramped up right after it."
D005-D018_h010.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Delusional Disorder

D005-D018_h011.question: "It all started about four months ago, right after... well, after the robbery at the bank. I was right there, you know, at the counter. Ever since, it’s like my mind plays tricks on me. I'll be walking down the street and see people whispering, and I just know they're talking about me, about what happened. It’s like their conversations are all directed at me, even though I logically know they couldn't be. Sometimes, it gets so bad, I’ll find myself frozen stiff, my arms up like I'm still trying to shield myself, even though nothing's happening. My husband tries to talk to me when I get like that, but it's like I’m reliving it – the sounds, the gun, everything. It’s not just a memory; it’s like I’m right back there, right in the middle of it again, even seeing things around me that aren't real, just like it was then. These aren't just random visions; they're always tied to that day, playing over and over."
D005-D018_h011.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Major Depressive Disorder

D005-D018_h012.question:
It’s been pretty rough lately, doc. For about four months now, I've just felt... off. I'm constantly on edge, and I can't shake the feeling that my girlfriend is seeing someone else. Every time she texts, I just know it's him, even though there's absolutely no proof. I find myself checking her phone, accusing her, and it’s pushing her away.

And then there are these moments, especially when I’m trying to edit videos from the accident. It’s like I’m right back there, seeing it all again, hearing the screams, even smelling the smoke. Sometimes a colleague will say something and I'll find myself repeating it back, exactly as they said it, without even meaning to. It’s not just scary; it's like a film reel playing in my head, very vivid, extremely realistic, making me truly believe I am right there again. The thing is, all this stuff, the visions, the repeating words, it all started  *after* the car crash I was in. I know those aren't real, but the terror is.
D005-D018_h012.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Major Depressive Disorder

D005-D018_h013.question:
"It's like I'm stuck in a constant loop, doctor. For the past four months, I’ve been having these… visions. Not just in my head, but around me. I’ll be sitting at home, and suddenly, I’m back *there*, hearing the sirens, the screaming from that pile-up a year ago, seeing bits of it in the room with me. It’s terrifying, but it’s always about *that*.

And the delusions… I keep thinking my ex-boyfriend is still out there, seeing other people, even though we broke up ages ago. It’s absurd, I know, to fuss over someone who’s not even in my life, and sometimes I'll say things that sound really goofy or just plain silly when I'm under stress, like a little kid. I'm also so jumpy now, simple car backfires will make me leap. It feels like my brain is replaying the worst parts of my job over and over, and I can't escape it."
D005-D018_h013.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Major Depressive Disorder

D005-D018_h014.question: It's been about four months since I started feeling truly off. After my husband passed, the house felt so empty, and then this... I'm seeing things, flashes mostly, of the accident, like I'm right back there. It's so real, sometimes I swear I can smell the smoke. And my body just locks up sometimes, I'll be in the middle of dusting and just hold a pose, unable to move for what feels like ages, like I'm frozen, remembering. I even started to believe I have some kind of special power now, that I can prevent bad things from happening if I just… if I just think about them hard enough, or hold my breath for a certain amount of time. It’s like these memories, they’re not just thoughts, they’re happening again, and somehow tied to this new purpose I feel I have to protect others.
D005-D018_h014.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Major Depressive Disorder

D005-D018_h015.question: "It's been... I don't even know, months now, maybe four or so, since I started feeling really off. After my husband, bless his soul, passed away so suddenly, I just haven't been right. I keep seeing him, clear as day, standing right there in the bakery, almost like he’s really there, talking to me. And then I’ll hear people talking nearby and I just repeat what they say without even thinking, like an echo. But what’s really been tearing me up inside is this terrible feeling, this absolute certainty, that he was cheating on me before he died. I go over every little thing in my head, convinced he had someone else, even though I know deep down it’s not true. I know he loved me. I try to tell myself that, but the image of him with someone else, it just plays in my mind, vivid as a movie. It’s like it’s happening again, constantly. It’s been happening ever since that awful day."
D005-D018_h015.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Major Depressive Disorder

D005-D018_h016.question: It’s been an absolute nightmare for the past three months. I can barely bring myself to speak most days, and when I do, I'm afraid people just hear rhymes and nonsense, not what I’m trying to say, like my words are all tangled. It all started after… that incident during the live broadcast. I keep feeling like ants are crawling under my skin, and some days, I’m convinced my heart is rotting inside my chest. It feels so real, like it’s actually happening. These feelings, especially the ants, they get so much worse when I remember *that day*, and it’s like I’m right back there in the anchor's chair, the lights, the chaos, feeling hands touching me when no one was there – it’s not just a memory, it's like it's happening all over again.
D005-D018_h016.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizophrenia

D005-D018_h017.question: It's been… I don't know, about three months now that things have felt really wrong. It all started after that terrible night at the café, when that guy tried to rob us. Ever since, it’s like my mind just won't let go. I keep tasting blood in my mouth, even when I haven't cut myself. And I know it sounds crazy, but I feel like I'm being watched all the time, especially when I'm alone in my apartment. Like the robbers are still out there, just waiting. Sometimes, when I try to explain it, the words just get all jumbled up, like a word salad, and I can't make sense. And honestly, it's hard to even get out of bed most days, let alone find the energy to look for a real job beyond a few barista shifts. But these intense moments, the tastes and the feeling of being watched, they always hit me when I'm reliving that night, seeing it all happen again as if it's real.
D005-D018_h017.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizophrenia

D005-D018_h018.question:
It’s all been a bit much, honestly. For about three months now, I’ve felt like everything is… different. Like, when I'm walking through the market, I see people whispering and looking at me, and I just know they're talking about *me*, about what happened. It’s like they all know. And then there are these creepy-crawly sensations, especially when I’m trying to relax at night, like bugs are just… on me, under my skin. It's not real, I know, but it feels so real.

When my wife asks me a question, I try to answer, but my mind just jumps around. I end up talking about something completely different, and then I realize I haven't even told her what she asked. It's made me want to just stay home, away from everyone. I used to love our dinner parties, but now the thought of small talk or company just feels impossible. It all started after the accident at work, the one where the new hire lost his hand. I keep seeing it, hearing it, and sometimes, it feels like I'm right back there, holding his arm, covered in blood. Those moments, they’re so vivid, like I'm reliving it with all my senses. Yet, even in those moments, I know it's not real, not really happening now. But it's always about *that*.
D005-D018_h018.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizophrenia

D005-D018_h019.question:
It’s been difficult to even come here, honestly. I keep seeing things… shadows, sometimes whole figures, in the corner of my eye. Last week, while teaching a lesson, I swore I saw a man in the window staring in, but when I looked again, there was nothing. It started about three months ago. I also hear whispers, sometimes my own name, but there’s no one there. And my thoughts… it feels like people are actively trying to hurt me, or watching everything I do. I constantly feel exposed. Then there’s how I talk sometimes, like "the bell fell, hell to tell, but well done, hun." It just comes out.

Ever since that accident – the car crash where I was hit by a drunk driver – it's been getting worse. I keep reliving it, seeing the headlights coming at me again and again. These aren't just memories, it feels like I'm right back there, the screech of metal, the smell of burning… it's so real, like it's happening all over again right in front of me. These visions, these delusions, they’re all mixed up with that night. Everything feels connected to that trauma. Beyond that, I just don't have the energy for anything anymore. My piano lessons feel like a monumental task, and I used to love them.
D005-D018_h019.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizophrenia

D005-D018_h020.question:
It’s hard to know where to begin, doctor. For the past three months, it feels like I’m living in a different world. After what happened during that storm, everything just shifted. I keep re-living it, flashes of the wind and the screams of people on the ground. Sometimes, it's so vivid I can taste the metallic, bitter air from that day, like it’s right there in my mouth. It’s not just memories; it’s like it’s happening again, right in front of me, even when I know I’m safe at home.

Lately, I’ve also started feeling like the news reports or even conversations on TV are secretly about me, hinting at what I went through, or blaming me. My wife tries to talk to me, but sometimes the words just get jumbled in my head, like a tangled mess of weather patterns, and I can't get them out coherently. It’s like my brain is stuck in a loop. I used to love my work, but now, I just… can't. I struggle to even get out of bed most days, let alone prepare a forecast. I just sit and stare, completely unable to start anything. I know it’s impacting my marriage, but I can’t seem to help it.
D005-D018_h020.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizophrenia

D005-D018_h021.question: Lately, things have been really off, Doc. It started about three months ago, shortly after what happened at that last estate sale – the one with the fire. Since then, I keep smelling burning wood, even when there's nothing there, and sometimes it's so strong I can almost feel the heat. It’s like it’s happening all over again. I’ve also noticed that the young woman who helps stage the items for my auctions, I’m quite certain she's fallen for me. The way she looks at me, the little smiles, it’s all very clear. I find myself standing in certain positions for no reason, like I'm frozen, unable to move until the smell fades, or the memories of the fire lessen. It’s really affecting my work; my wife has noticed I’m not myself. My mind keeps replaying that day, and these smells and feelings are always tied back to it.
D005-D018_h021.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D018_h022.question: "Well, doctor, it all started after that terrible car accident, just over three months ago. My husband didn't make it, and I've not been right since. It’s like my body is reliving it all, right alongside my mind falling to pieces."
D005-D018_h022.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia

D005-D018_h023.question:
It’s been, what, three months now? Since the storm. The big one. That's when things really went sideways. I barely remember the immediate aftermath, just kind of… existing. Like I wasn’t really there, you know? Like my body was moving, but my mind was… blank.

Now, it’s like the world is teetering on the edge. I keep tasting ash, like everything's already burned up. A bitter, metallic taste that won't go away. I see the waves crash against the rocks, and it's not just water anymore. It’s like the whole structure, the lighthouse itself, is crumbling, and the end is coming right for me. I try to tell myself it's just the stress, that it's all tied to that night, but it feels so real, like the world is truly ending. The smells, the sounds, the feeling of the spray... it’s like I’m right back in the middle of it.
D005-D018_h023.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D018_h024.question: Lately, it's been hard to focus on work, even with the Webtoons I used to love drawing.
